---
title: viewTransition
description: Enable ViewTransition API from React in App Router
version: experimental
---

`viewTransition` enables React's [View Transitions API](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/View_Transition_API) integration in Next.js. This lets you animate navigations, loading states, and content changes using the native browser View Transitions API.

To enable this feature, you need to set the `viewTransition` property to `true` in your `next.config.js` file.

```js filename="next.config.js"
/** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */
const nextConfig = {
  experimental: {
    viewTransition: true,
  },
}

module.exports = nextConfig
```

> [!NOTE]
> The [`<ViewTransition>`](https://react.dev/reference/react/ViewTransition) component is provided by React.
> The `experimental.viewTransition` flag enables Next.js integration, such as triggering
> transitions during route navigations.

## Usage

You can import the [`<ViewTransition>` Component](https://react.dev/reference/react/ViewTransition) from React in your application:

```jsx
import { ViewTransition } from 'react'
```

### Live Demo

Check out the [View Transitions Demo](https://react-view-transitions-demo.labs.vercel.dev) to see this feature in action, or read the [designing view transitions guide](/docs/app/guides/view-transitions) for a step-by-step walkthrough.

The View Transitions API is a baseline web standard, and browser support continues to expand. As React's [`<ViewTransition>`](https://react.dev/reference/react/ViewTransition) component evolves, more transition patterns and use cases will become available.

events.content:
Here’s what was implemented:

### Config
- **`next.config.ts`** — `experimental.viewTransition: true` so route changes run as React transitions and drive `<ViewTransition>`.

### Shared hero morph
- **`ProductGrid.tsx`** — Each card’s image block is wrapped in `<ViewTransition name={\`product-${slug}\`} share="morph">`. Links use **`transitionTypes={['nav-forward']}`**.
- **`app/product/[slug]/page.tsx`** — The hero uses the same **`name`** and **`share="morph"`** so the thumbnail and detail hero are one shared-element transition.

### Directional page motion
- **Home** and **product** pages wrap the sliding area (grid / product detail) in `<ViewTransition>` with **`enter` / `exit`** maps for **`nav-forward`** and **`nav-back`** (other cases use **`default: 'none'`** so the first load doesn’t animate).
- **Back link** uses **`transitionTypes={['nav-back']}`**.

### Suspense skeleton → content
- **`Suspense`** fallbacks use **`<ViewTransition exit="slide-down">`**
- Resolved children use **`<ViewTransition enter="slide-up" default="none">`** so skeleton handoff animates without fighting the shared-element morph.

### Fixed header (directional slides)
- **`site-header`** class sets **`view-transition-name: site-header`** and **`globals.css`** disables group animation for **`site-header`** so the top chrome stays stable while content moves.

### CSS (`globals.css`)
- Morph timing + **`via-blur`** on **`::view-transition-image-pair(.morph)`**
- **`slide-up` / `slide-down`** (fade + short vertical move) for Suspense
- **`nav-forward` / `nav-back`** horizontal slides + fades
- **`@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)`** — zero duration/delay on view-transition animations **and** turns off skeleton **pulse**

Build completes successfully with **`✓ viewTransition`** enabled.

Here’s what was implemented:

### Config
- **`next.config.ts`** — `experimental.viewTransition: true` so route changes run as React transitions and drive `<ViewTransition>`.

### Shared hero morph
- **`ProductGrid.tsx`** — Each card’s image block is wrapped in `<ViewTransition name={\`product-${slug}\`} share="morph">`. Links use **`transitionTypes={['nav-forward']}`**.
- **`app/product/[slug]/page.tsx`** — The hero uses the same **`name`** and **`share="morph"`** so the thumbnail and detail hero are one shared-element transition.

### Directional page motion
- **Home** and **product** pages wrap the sliding area (grid / product detail) in `<ViewTransition>` with **`enter` / `exit`** maps for **`nav-forward`** and **`nav-back`** (other cases use **`default: 'none'`** so the first load doesn’t animate).
- **Back link** uses **`transitionTypes={['nav-back']}`**.

### Suspense skeleton → content
- **`Suspense`** fallbacks use **`<ViewTransition exit="slide-down">`**
- Resolved children use **`<ViewTransition enter="slide-up" default="none">`** so skeleton handoff animates without fighting the shared-element morph.

### Fixed header (directional slides)
- **`site-header`** class sets **`view-transition-name: site-header`** and **`globals.css`** disables group animation for **`site-header`** so the top chrome stays stable while content moves.

### CSS (`globals.css`)
- Morph timing + **`via-blur`** on **`::view-transition-image-pair(.morph)`**
- **`slide-up` / `slide-down`** (fade + short vertical move) for Suspense
- **`nav-forward` / `nav-back`** horizontal slides + fades
- **`@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)`** — zero duration/delay on view-transition animations **and** turns off skeleton **pulse**
